items.title: British Pound futures climb on UK inflation and rate hike expectations.
items.excerpt: British Pound futures moved higher for the fourth session in the last five, rising 1.63% since the October 14 close. Prices traded near their highest closing levels since mid-September as market expectations for a November Bank of England rate hike strengthened. UK consumer prices rose 3.5% year-over-year in September, exceeding the 3.4% forecast and accelerating from 3.1% in August, driven by a 29.8% jump in motor fuel prices and a 3.7% increase in services inflation. Additionally, UK unemployment fell to 4.7% in the three months through August, coming in below the 4.9% expectation. Interest rate markets are now pricing in a 95% probability of a rate hike to 4% on November 5, providing structural support for the currency ahead of the UK budget announcement.

items.title: CoreWeave after the bond scare: what a cash-secured put pays for, and what it carries
items.excerpt: CoreWeave shares fell about a quarter in a month as its bonds traded at distressed yields. Puts now pay more than usual. What does a cash-secured put seller get paid for, and what does the seller take on? When a company s bonds come under pressure, its puts get more expensive. The seller collects more, and takes on more. CoreWeave (CRWV on Nasdaq), which rents out computing power for AI, has had a hard month. Its shares closed at USD 62.13 on 20 October 2026, about a quarter lower than a month earlier and not far above their lowest level of the past year (Source: Saxo). Past performance is not indicative of future results. Most of the damage came on 14 October, when the shares lost more than 15% in one session. items.title: Roche sales update: buying lower or selling higher, and being paid to wait
items.excerpt: Roche reports its nine-month sales on 22 October 2026, after a rise of about 9% since July. One investor wants to buy lower, another already owns the shares. How can each name a price and be paid to wait? Before a company reports, options on its shares tend to cost more than in a quiet week. Whoever sells the option collects that extra. Roche publishes its nine-month sales on Thursday 22 October 2026 at 07:00 CET, before the Swiss market opens. The shares closed at CHF 380.10, about 9% higher than after the July results (Source: Saxo price data, as of 19 October 2026). Markets look ahead to Federal Reserve speakers Kevin Warsh and Beth Hammack for any signal on inflation and interest rates before the next FOMC meeting.
